import numpy as np
from scipy import stats
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
from sklearn.feature_selection import mutual_info_classif
from collections import defaultdict

MAX_DRIVERS = 5

def design(feats):
    # Find features with significant association (p < 0.05)
    ids = list(feats.ids)
    p_values = [stats.ttest_ind(feats.x[feats.y==1, feats.column(id)], 
                               feats.x[feats.y==0, feats.column(id)], 
                               equal_var=False)[1] 
                for id in ids]
    
    # Select features with p < 0.05 and strong effect size
    sig_features = [id for id, p in zip(ids, p_values) if p < 0.05]
    
    # Check for correlated pairs (|r| >= 0.6) and remove near-duplicates
    corr_pairs = []
    for i, id1 in enumerate(sig_features):
        for j, id2 in enumerate(sig_features[i+1:], i+1):
            r = np.corrcoef(feats.x[:, feats.column(id1)], 
                           feats.x[:, feats.column(id2)])[0,1]
            if abs(r) >= 0.6:
                corr_pairs.append((id1, id2))
    
    # Remove near-duplicates, keeping the one with higher mean_y1-mean_y0
    keep_features = set()
    for id1, id2 in corr_pairs:
        if id1 not in keep_features and id2 not in keep_features:
            # Choose the one with stronger effect
            eff1 = np.mean(feats.x[feats.y==1, feats.column(id1)]) - \
                   np.mean(feats.x[feats.y==0, feats.column(id1)])
            eff2 = np.mean(feats.x[feats.y==1, feats.column(id2)]) - \
                   np.mean(feats.x[feats.y==0, feats.column(id2)])
            keep_features.add(id1 if abs(eff1) > abs(eff2) else id2)
    
    # Add non-correlated features
    for id in sig_features:
        if id not in keep_features:
            keep_features.add(id)
    
    # Check for interaction terms
    candidates = list(keep_features)
    best_interaction = None
    best_p = 1.0
    
    # Try all pairs of features to find significant interactions
    for i, id1 in enumerate(candidates):
        for j, id2 in enumerate(candidates[i+1:], i+1):
            # Create interaction term
            x1 = feats.x[:, feats.column(id1)]
            x2 = feats.x[:, feats.column(id2)]
            interaction = x1 * x2
            
            # Fit logistic regression with interaction
            X = np.column_stack([x1, x2, interaction])
            model = LogisticRegression(fit_intercept=True, max_iter=1000)
            model.fit(X, feats.y)
            
            # Get p-value for interaction term
            coef = model.coef_[0]
            se = np.linalg.inv(np.dot(X.T, X)) @ np.diag(coef**2)
            t_stat = coef[-1] / np.sqrt(se[-1,-1]) if se[-1,-1] > 0 else 0
            p_val = 2 * (1 - stats.t.cdf(abs(t_stat), len(feats.y) - 3))
            
            if p_val < best_p:
                best_p = p_val
                best_interaction = (id1, id2)
    
    # If we found a significant interaction, return it
    if best_interaction and best_p < 0.05:
        return Design(
            drivers=(best_interaction[0], best_interaction[1]),
            columns=(best_interaction[0], best_interaction[1]),
            products=(best_interaction,),
            loadings={}
        )
    
    # Otherwise, look for single drivers using mutual information
    mi_scores = mutual_info_classif(feats.x[:, [feats.column(id) for id in candidates]], feats.y)
    sorted_indices = np.argsort(mi_scores)[::-1][:MAX_DRIVERS]
    drivers = tuple([candidates[i] for i in sorted_indices if mi_scores[i] > 0])
    
    # Return single drivers if any, otherwise empty
    if drivers:
        return Design(
            drivers=drivers,
            columns=drivers,
            products=(),
            loadings={}
        )
    else:
        return Design(
            drivers=(),
            columns=(),
            products=(),
            loadings={}
        )
